transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. I guess what made me come in is that I just keep feeling like I ruined things for everybody. I'm in a pipefitting apprenticeship, and lately I just feel like a total fake in the program. Like I'm letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices down, over stuff that... well, I know other people would probably just fix the issue and move on from it. But I just can't seem to do that.
Did this start after a specific stressful event?

Not really. I mean, there wasn't one big thing that happened. It just sort of... crept up on me, I guess. I've just been feeling this way more and more lately, without any real reason for it to start.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?

Um, no, I don't think so. I wouldn't really say I feel sad or depressed most days. It's... well, it's really just that feeling of being a fake and messing things up that I mentioned. But I don't really feel down in the way you mean, no.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

Not really, no. I wouldn't say I'm a worrier. I mean, I don't just sit around stressing about random things for no reason. It's really just... tied to that feeling of being a fake at the apprenticeship and letting everyone down. But outside of that specific stuff, I don't really worry a lot.
Has this been making it hard for you to do your job or apprenticeship duties?

Yeah, it has. Um, my instructors and my foreman have actually had to chase me down lately about unfinished sketches and just... my work being a lot slower than usual. I'm really scared that I'm getting close to damaging this apprenticeship, and the certification that I worked really hard to get.
Even if you wouldn’t call it depression, have you been feeling down or low in mood lately?

Um, no, not really. I know you're asking again, but it's honestly not like a general low mood. It's just... I feel bad about how I'm doing at work, and that really stresses me out. But I don't just wake up feeling down or sad in general.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Um... lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook, or skip playing volleyball, and I just ignore my volunteer group texts without really feeling much of anything. It's strange, because those used to be the things that made me feel like myself, but right now I just don't have much interest in them.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately?

Yeah, my sleep has definitely changed. Um, for a while there, I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours a night, but I'd still show up to the job site and my classes completely wired and ready to go. But lately... it's different. Now I just can't seem to fall asleep, or I'll wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just feel like I didn't get any rest at all.
During that time when you were sleeping only three or four hours a night, did you feel unusually up or euphoric?

Yeah, I did. Um, there were a few weeks where I felt almost too good... like Miami was just mine. But it wasn't just feeling great. If a coworker on the site slowed me down, even just a little comment from them would make me snap way harder than I normally would.
During those weeks when you felt unusually good and slept only a few hours, were you more active than usual or taking on a lot more projects?

Yeah, I definitely was. I just had this... like a nonstop charge in my body. After a full day working on pipes, I would still go to my evening classes, and then come home and reorganize all my tools. I'd clean my whole apartment, or start drawing out pipe systems instead of just sitting down and relaxing. I just couldn't really stop moving.
During that time, did you feel more powerful, important, or talented than usual?

Yeah, I actually did. Um, I honestly thought I could design something better than the instructors in my classes and even the senior guys on the job site. I just felt like... I don't know, like I was about to change how every building in Miami handled water. I really believed I had it all figured out, if people would just listen to me.
During that time when you felt unusually energized and powerful, did it get so severe that you had to be hospitalized?
No, no, nothing like that. I didn't go to the hospital or anything. I just... kept working and going to class. It never got to the point where I needed to be admitted.
